description: Letterbox preprocessing WITH A NON-EMPTY PADDING BAND, issue #33. The existing preprocess fixture feeds a square image, so it has no padding at all and pins nothing about what padding contains. A 64x36 source into 64x64 has 28 padded rows -- 43.75% of the tensor -- and the value in them changes detections near the frame edge without changing anything that raises.

input.note: 16:9, the shape a 480p video proxy actually is. Already at its scaled size, so resampling is the identity and padding is the only thing under test -- see the module docstring for why resampling is not pinned.

pad_value.source: opencv/opencv modules/objdetect/src/face_detect.cpp, FaceDetectorYNImpl::padWithDivisor: copyMakeBorder(..., BORDER_CONSTANT, 0) -- the runtime every published YuNet number is measured through. Agreed by the training repository: ShiqiYu/libfacedetection.train yunet_train/tasks/face/transforms.py::build_eval_transforms uses Pad(size=(image_size,image_size), pad_value=0) followed by Normalize(mean=0, std=1), and the size_divisor variant uses pad_value=0 too. Because this config has scale 1 with empty mean and std, pixel 0 and tensor 0.0 coincide, so the two spaces agree here as well.

applied.order: (pixel * scale - mean) / std, band included when space is 'pixel'

counter_cases.note: The same image and the same geometry with the two other padding values the runtime could plausibly have invented. Every number below is a valid tensor; nothing here would raise. This block is what makes the fixture a test rather than a restatement of the code.
